guideTitle: 6 Best Non Slip Shower Mats in 2026
metaTitle: Best Non Slip Shower Mats in 2026
metaDescription: Six non slip shower and tub mats compared by suction cup count, drain holes, material, size and cleaning, with the surface checks that decide if suction works.
introParagraphs: A non slip shower mat is the cheapest piece of bathroom safety equipment and one of the easiest to get wrong. The mat has to grip your feet on top and grip the tub floor underneath, and both jobs depend on details a product photo cannot show: the number and size of suction cups, the way drain holes let water escape, the softness of the material and, above all, whether your tub surface is smooth enough for suction to hold at all.

The six mats here are the GORILLA GRIP 35 by 16 inch with hundreds of suction cups and a hexagon pebble top, the OTHWAY with 198 suction cups and 360 drain holes in TPE, the TEMIR that cites ASTM F462 wet-surface slip testing, the TEESHLY 40 by 16 inch with a domed top, the homerella 35 by 16 inch with over 250 cups and the BEMISO 27.5 by 15.7 inch TPE and PP mat with over 160 cups.

We evaluated each on grip design, drainage, material, size and how easy it is to keep clean. Suction mats only hold on smooth, non-porous surfaces, so every pick here assumes a smooth tub or shower floor, and the sections below point to alternatives for textured surfaces. A mat reduces slipping risk underfoot, but it does not eliminate it, so combine it with a grab bar and careful stepping.

products.name: GORILLA GRIP Bath Tub Shower Mat, 35x16 Clear
products.description:
GORILLA GRIP's tub mat is the familiar benchmark: a 35 by 16 inch liner with hundreds of suction cups on the underside and hundreds of drainage holes that let water run toward the drain. The listing says the patented design keeps the mat in place and that it is built from BPA-free materials, machine washable, with a hexagon pattern and a pebble-textured top. The clear version is the one reviewed here.

The combination of cups and drain holes addresses the two ways a mat fails: sliding, and trapping water that breeds mildew. The pebble top gives bare feet a grippy but not harsh surface, and the machine-washable construction means you can launder it instead of scrubbing the cups. The listing does not state a cup count in the text we have, so we do not quote one.

Compared with the OTHWAY it gives a stated size and a recognizable brand but fewer numbers, and compared with the TEESHLY it is a little shorter. It suits a standard tub with a smooth floor where a reliable, no-fuss mat is wanted. A new mat should be rinsed, pressed down firmly and left for a few minutes to seal before the first shower.
products.bestFor: A standard smooth tub and a dependable, washable mat.
pros: Hundreds of suction cups hold the mat in place
cons: Cup count is not stated in the text we have
Needs a smooth, non-porous tub floor

products.name: OTHWAY Non Slip Bath Tub Shower Mat, 198 Suction Cups
products.description:
OTHWAY is the listing that gives the most numbers: 198 high-density suction cups, 360 precision-angled drain holes and a flexible TPE body with raised nodules. The listing contrasts its 360 holes with 250 on standard mats, claiming faster water removal. TPE is a soft, durable, low-odor material that flexes like a mat should.

Stated counts are a help to a buyer, because suction mats are only as good as their contact with the floor, and more cups spread the hold across more of the surface. Drain holes matter for hygiene, since a mat that dries between showers grows less mildew. The raised nodules add a gentle massage feel under the feet, and the flexible TPE conforms to a slightly curved tub floor.

Compared with the GORILLA GRIP it states its cup and hole counts, and compared with the BEMISO it has more of both. It suits a buyer who likes to see the numbers behind a mat and wants quick drainage. If your tub has a tiny dip near the drain, a flexible TPE body helps the cups find the floor.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want stated cup and drain counts and quick drainage.
cons: Dimensions are not stated in the text we have
Nodules may feel firm to sensitive feet

products.name: TEMIR Non Slip Bathtub Mat With Strong Suction Cups

specList.label: Testing
specList.value: ASTM F462 wet slip, per listing

products.description:
TEMIR attaches a specific standard to its claim: the listing says the mat was tested in a U.S.-based accredited lab following ASTM F462 wet-surface slip resistance guidelines. It also describes strong suction cups for smooth bathtub and shower bases, quick drain holes and a textured surface that is soft on bare feet. A named test is more informative than the word safe alone.

A standard gives a reference, but a listing's testing statement is still the maker's claim, so read it as design intent and check the exact scope on the product page. The textured, soft surface aims for grip without hardness, and the machine-washable construction handles cleaning. The listing says the mat is designed for clean, smooth surfaces.

Compared with the GORILLA GRIP it cites a standard, and compared with the OTHWAY it gives no cup or hole counts in the text we have. It suits a buyer who wants a named test behind the grip and a soft feel underfoot. If you want to double-check the scope of the test, the product page is the place to find the exact conditions cited.
products.bestFor: A mat with a named wet-slip test reference.
pros: ASTM F462 wet-surface slip testing cited
Strong suction cups for smooth surfaces
cons: Testing statement is the maker's claim
Cup and hole counts are not stated in the text we have

products.name: TEESHLY Non Slip Bath Tub and Shower Mat, 40 x 16 Inch
products.description:
TEESHLY covers more of the tub: 40 by 16 inches, longer than the 35-inch mats, with a domed pebble-like surface that the listing says gives a massage-like feel and drain holes for water flow. It is made of soft-touch PVC and is machine washable. The extra length matters in a long tub where a shorter mat leaves bare floor at the ends.

Coverage is the main benefit, since a mat that spans most of the tub floor gives your feet more places to land and reduces the gaps where you could slip. PVC is a durable, low-cost material, though it is less flexible than TPE. The listing does not state a suction cup count in the text we have.

Compared with the GORILLA GRIP it is five inches longer, and compared with the homerella it is longer but with fewer stated cups. It suits a long tub where coverage is the priority. On a long tub, it also helps to center the mat under the showerhead so that the ends do not curl.
products.bestFor: Long tubs that need more floor coverage.
pros: 40 in length covers more of the tub
cons: Cup count is not stated in the text we have
PVC is less flexible than TPE
Long mat may not fit short or curved tubs

products.name: homerella Non Slip Bathtub Mat, 35x16, Mildew Resistant
products.description:
homerella states more than 250 anti-slip suction cups on the bottom of a 35 by 16 inch mat, an anti-mold and mildew resistant design that is machine washable on a cold cycle, and an odorless material. The listing says the mat suits sensitive skin and is made for everyone including babies, older adults and pregnant users. A high cup count is its headline.

More suction cups spread the hold across the floor, which can help on a tub with slight irregularities. A cold machine wash is a convenient way to clean the cups and the mat, and it reduces the mildew that builds under suction mats. The listing's claims about antibacterial properties are the maker's wording.

Compared with the OTHWAY it has a higher stated cup count but a smaller stated drain count, and compared with the GORILLA GRIP it gives the cup number. It suits a buyer who wants many cups and an easy cold wash. Cold water and a gentle cycle keep the cups from deforming in the wash.
products.bestFor: A high cup count and a simple cold-wash routine.
cons: Antibacterial claims are the maker's wording
Drain hole count is not stated in the text we have

products.name: BEMISO Non Slip Bathtub Mat, 27.5 x 15.7 Inch, Drain Holes
products.description:
BEMISO is the compact option at 27.5 by 15.7 inches, made of TPE and PP with over 160 suction cups and slotted panels that let soapy water pass through quickly. The listing calls the material eco-friendly and comfortable to the touch and pitches it for babies and older adults alike. The smaller size suits a narrow tub or a standing shower with limited floor space.

A smaller mat covers less floor, so it is a better fit when the main need is a defined standing spot, such as under the showerhead. Slotted panels dry quickly, which helps with mildew. The cup count is lower than the others, which is proportional to the size.

Compared with the TEESHLY it is shorter by more than ten inches, and compared with the OTHWAY it has fewer cups. It suits a small tub or a shower stall where a large mat will not fit. If the tub is a combination unit, measure the flat section of the floor and leave a margin at the walls.
products.bestFor: Narrow tubs and small shower floors.
cons: Covers less floor than larger mats

buyingCriteria.explanation: Suction cups only hold on smooth, non-porous surfaces, so every mat in this guide assumes a smooth tub floor. Textured, grouted or refinished surfaces prevent a seal and let the mat drift. Press your palm on the tub floor and feel for texture. If it is bumpy, skip suction and look at weighted or non-suction mats.

The homerella lists over 250 cups, the OTHWAY 198, the BEMISO over 160 and the GORILLA GRIP and TEMIR list hundreds or strong cups without a figure. Wider, flatter cups tend to seal better than narrow ones, and a spread across the mat resists lifting at the edges. A high count is good, but sealing on a clean, flat floor matters more than the number. A flat, clean floor and a firm press matter more than another fifty cups on the label.

The OTHWAY lists 360 holes and the GORILLA GRIP lists hundreds, while others use slotted panels. Good drainage keeps water from pooling under the mat, which is where mildew grows. Even so, lift the mat after each shower to let the floor dry. Holes help, but habits matter more.

TPE on the OTHWAY and BEMISO is soft, flexible and low-odor, while PVC on the TEESHLY is durable and slightly stiffer. A softer mat is kinder to bare feet, and a flexible one conforms to a curved tub. Rubber can smell at first. Pick the feel you prefer.

Sizes here run from 27.5 inches on the BEMISO to 40 inches on the TEESHLY. A long mat covers more of the tub, and a short one fits tight spaces. Measure your flat floor area, not the tub's top dimensions. Curved edges can lift the mat.

The homerella and TEMIR list machine washing, and the GORILLA GRIP is machine washable. Washing on a cold cycle and hanging to dry reduces mildew. Rinse soap film from the cups, which trap grime. A mat you can clean easily is a mat you will clean. Run a hand along the underside after washing to check that no soap film remains on the cups.

howWeEvaluated.title: Grip design
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared suction cup counts and claims: over 250 on the homerella, 198 on the OTHWAY and over 160 on the BEMISO. We also looked at surface texture, from the GORILLA GRIP hexagon pebbles to the TEESHLY domes. Stated numbers earned credit. We read cup and hole counts as helpful indicators, and weighed them below how well the mat is likely to seal on a clean, smooth floor.

howWeEvaluated.title: Drainage
howWeEvaluated.description: Drain holes and slotted panels were compared, with the OTHWAY 360 holes standing out. We considered how drainage affects mildew. Listings that omit counts were flagged. Where a listing quoted a standard or a test, we noted it as the maker's statement.

howWeEvaluated.title: Material and feel
howWeEvaluated.description: TPE, PVC and PP were compared for softness, flexibility and odor. We considered how each feels underfoot. Softer, flexible materials earned credit for comfort. Size claims were checked against the sizes buyers say they need for common tubs.

howWeEvaluated.title: Size and fit
howWeEvaluated.description: Sizes from 27.5 to 40 inches were compared and matched to tub types. We noted that a mat must fit the flat floor area. Coverage and fit counted. We considered how easy each mat is to clean, since a mat that is hard to wash is likely to be neglected.

howWeEvaluated.title: Cleaning ease and claims
howWeEvaluated.description: Machine washability and mildew-resistance claims were compared. The TEMIR ASTM F462 statement was read as a maker's claim. We favored mats that are easy to wash and dry. Comfort underfoot was part of the evaluation, because a mat that feels harsh may be removed.

faq.q: Will a suction mat work in my tub?
faq.a: Only on smooth, non-porous surfaces. Textured, grouted or refinished floors prevent a seal. Press your hand on the floor to feel for texture. If it is bumpy, look at non-suction or weighted mats. Warm water and a little dish soap loosen oils that build up on the tub floor, which is the most common reason a suction mat stops gripping.

faq.q: How do I clean a suction mat?
faq.a: Machine wash on cold if the listing allows, or scrub with mild soap, then hang to dry. Lift it after each shower to dry the floor beneath. Rinse soap film from the cups. Textured tub bottoms are common in older bathrooms and some refinished tubs, so it pays to test before assuming suction will work.

The tub floor may be textured, dirty or oily from soap and bath oil. Clean the floor and the cups, press the mat down and let it settle. If it still slides, the surface may not suit suction. If a mat curls at the edges, a few minutes in the sun or a rinse with warm water usually relaxes it.

Yes, because water trapped under a mat grows mildew. The OTHWAY lists 360 holes and the GORILLA GRIP lists hundreds. Still, lift the mat to dry the tub. Lifting the mat after each shower seems like a chore but keeps the cups sealing and the floor clean.

faq.q: How often should I replace a mat?
faq.a: When the cups lose their grip, the surface wears smooth or mildew stains will not wash out. Many mats last a year or two with regular cleaning. Replace a mat that slides. Some people keep a second mat so that one can dry while the other is in use.

faq.q: Is a mat enough for safety?
faq.a: A mat reduces slipping underfoot but does not eliminate it. Pair it with a grab bar and careful stepping. A therapist can advise on a safer setup for specific needs. A mat is a good foundation, but good lighting and a grab bar also make the bath safer.
